hints.title: Huffman Greedy Merge Property
hints.text: Merging two lists of lengths a and b costs a + b. To minimize the overall cost, always greedily merge the two shortest available lists.

hints.title: Priority Queue for Lengths
hints.text: Insert the lengths of all lists into a min-priority queue.

hints.title: Iterative Extraction and Insertion
hints.text: Repeatedly extract the two smallest lengths, sum them, add the sum to the total cost, and insert the sum back into the queue until one element remains.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import heapq

class Solution:
    def minMergeCost(self, lists: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        if len(lists) <= 1:
            return 0
        
        pq = [len(lst) for lst in lists]
        heapq.heapify(pq)
        
        total_cost = 0
        while len(pq) > 1:
            a = heapq.heappop(pq)
            b = heapq.heappop(pq)
            merged = a + b
            total_cost += merged
            heapq.heappush(pq, merged)
        return total_cost
```

complexity.notes: Here k is the number of lists.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Merging sequentially from left to right can result in quadratic O(k^2) merge cost.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Heap of size k uses O(k) memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Expects standard Huffman / optimal merge tree application with min-heap.
